rules.rule: Preload is the only renderer/main boundary. Check that every bridge function passes a narrow, validated argument shape, that no Node primitive (fs, child_process, ipcRenderer) leaks onto `window`, and that the IPC channel names match the ones the main process registers. A widened bridge surface here is a renderer-side sandbox escape.

Electron main-process code. Flag: unvalidated IPC payload handling, `shell.openExternal` / `openPath` on non-allowlisted values, path traversal in any file dialog or handler, secrets written to logs or crash reports, and missing `contextIsolation` / `nodeIntegration` hardening on new BrowserWindow or WebContentsView construction.

This module is the canonical frontend path helper surface. Verify new path handling is routed through the existing helpers rather than open-coding `path.join` with user input. Flag any new absolute-path construction that skips the helpers or bypasses the agent-scoped permission check.

Main-process HTTP/IPC handlers. Flag unvalidated request bodies, path traversal, missing per-agent file permission enforcement on every tool path (not just the global workspace setting), SSRF in any outbound fetch, and secrets echoed into responses or logs.

IPC handler module. Every exported handler must validate its input before use, enforce the effective agent file scope on any path argument, and return a serializable value. Flag handlers that trust client-supplied paths, scopes, or model identifiers.

TypeScript / React. Focus on real defects over style: incorrect null handling and unhandled promise rejections, React hook dependency and cleanup bugs, stale closures, unsafe `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` or unsanitized HTML injection, and state updates on unmounted components. Prefer calling out a missing cleanup or a wrong dependency over restating formatting.

JavaScript / TypeScript. Look for prototype-pollution sinks, unvalidated `JSON.parse` of untrusted input, regexes with catastrophic backtracking, TOCTOU races in file operations, and secrets or tokens hardcoded or written to logs.

Build or release script. Flag destructive operations without a confirmation or dry-run guard, unpinned or unverified remote downloads (no checksum/signature check), secrets passed on the command line where they land in process listings or CI logs, and anything that would publish or push without explicit authorization.

Electron packaging entry point. Review for changes that widen what gets bundled or signed, alter signing or publishing behavior, or bypass the license/attribution checks. Any behavior that publishes an artifact must be flagged.

Test file. Only flag a real problem: a test that asserts nothing meaningful, mocks away the very behavior under test, depends on execution order or wall-clock time, or would pass even if the production code were broken.
Configuration file. Check for committed credentials or tokens, machine-specific absolute paths, and dependency version ranges that would silently resolve to a different minor than intended.
